title: [Setup] Initialize the GitHub repository, basic CI/CD and Docker Compose environment
body:
## Objective
Set up the local infrastructure and the repository collaboration rules.

## Tasks
- Create the GitHub repository with `main` branch protection (PR required before merge).
- Add a Pull Request template (`.github/pull_request_template.md`).
- Configure `docker-compose.yml` with PostgreSQL and Redis.

## Acceptance Criteria (Done when)
- The `main` branch is protected.
- `docker compose up` starts PostgreSQL and Redis without errors.
milestone: Week 1: Understand brief and set up

title: [Analysis] Analyze the PayTrack PDF and define the 5 acceptance criteria
body:
## Objective
Extract the key requirements from the PayTrack specification and document the client's specific rule.

## Tasks
- Read the PayTrack requirements PDF.
- Write the list of 5 acceptance criteria in the Team Workspace.
- Confirm the client's additional rule (Ananya Keshwala - Thornbury Sallow Infrastructure: mandatory valid PO/Tender number and budget cap check before issuance) and add it as a User Story on the board.

## Acceptance Criteria (Done when)
- The 5 acceptance criteria are published in the workspace.
- The client PO/Tender rule is added to the board.

title: [Docs] Write the draft technical design document (/docs/design.md)
body:
## Objective
Write the architecture and technical specification document ready for mentor review by Nov 15.

## Tasks
- Create `/docs/design.md` with the sections: Architecture, Data Model, API Contract, Tax Rule, Numbering Rule, Risks.
- Complete the permission matrix first with the 5 roles from `FR-1.01` against each action.
- Detail the rounding rule and the numbering rule clearly and in a way that can be applied manually.

## Acceptance Criteria (Done when)
- All required sections are present in `/docs/design.md`.
- The permission matrix crosses the 5 roles and all actions.
- The rounding and numbering rules are manually verifiable.
- Ready for mentor review on Nov 15.
milestone: Week 1: Understand brief and set up

title: [DB/CI] Create the Flyway V1 multi-tenant migration and the Testcontainers CI pipeline
body:
## Objective
Structure the database for tenant isolation and automate integration tests.

## Tasks
- Add the Flyway `V1` migration, mandatorily including `organisation_id` on every table.
- Configure GitHub Actions to run integration tests with Testcontainers (PostgreSQL).

## Acceptance Criteria (Done when)
- The V1 migration applies cleanly.
- Every table has an `organisation_id` column.
- CI passes with Testcontainers PostgreSQL.
milestone: Week 2: Walking skeleton and core models

title: [Security] Implement Spring Security authentication and organisation isolation
body:
## Objective
Set up the secure Walking Skeleton with password hashing and strict data isolation per organisation.

## Tasks
- Add the Spring Security dependency to the Spring Boot project.
- Create a Flyway seed script with a test organisation and user (password hashed with BCrypt).
- Filter all queries by the `organisation_id` of the authenticated user.
- Test the connection locally with `curl` or Bruno.

## Acceptance Criteria (Done when)
- Login with the seeded user succeeds.
- A user from organisation A cannot see any data from organisation B.
- Passwords are stored as hashes in the database.
milestone: Week 2: Walking skeleton and core models

title: [Feature] Develop the Customer CRUD with GSTIN format validation
body:
## Objective
Manage each organisation's customers with tax validation and addresses.

## Tasks
- Create the CRUD endpoints for the `Customer` entity (including billing and shipping addresses).
- Implement strict GSTIN format validation.
- Write an integration test for each protected endpoint.

## Acceptance Criteria (Done when)
- Full CRUD is functional and isolated by `organisation_id`.
- Invalid GSTINs are rejected with a 400 error.
- Each protected endpoint is covered by an automated test.
milestone: Week 2: Walking skeleton and core models

title: [Feature] Implement invoice drafts and total calculations (BigDecimal)
body:
## Objective
Allow creating draft invoices with line items and exact server-side calculations.

## Tasks
- Create the models and endpoints for invoices (`Invoice`) and invoice line items (`InvoiceLineItem`).
- Calculate all subtotals, taxes and totals server-side with `BigDecimal`, strictly applying the rounding rule documented in `/docs/design.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria (Done when)
- Totals are calculated exclusively server-side via `BigDecimal`.
- Rounding complies with the technical specification.

title: [Feature] Implement the tax calculation engine (CGST/SGST vs IGST)
body:
## Objective
Automatically apply Indian GST rules based on the supplier's and customer's state.

## Tasks
- Implement `CGST` + `SGST` calculation for intra-state transactions (same state).
- Implement `IGST` calculation for inter-state transactions (different states).
- Write unit/integration tests verifying 3 manually calculated invoices.

## Acceptance Criteria (Done when)
- CGST/SGST and IGST are correctly applied based on the address.
- Tests pass on the 3 manually verified invoice cases.
labels: backend, feature, tax, testing, week-3, priority:high

title: [Feature] Implement locked sequential numbering per financial year
body:
## Objective
Guarantee consecutive invoice numbers with no duplicates or gaps in a concurrent environment.

## Tasks
- Create the management of numbering series per financial year (`Financial Year`).
- Use a pessimistic lock (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) on the series row at issuance.
- Write a concurrency test simulating 20 parallel issuances.

## Acceptance Criteria (Done when)
- 20 simultaneous issuances generate exactly 20 consecutive numbers without concurrency errors.
labels: backend, feature, concurrency, testing, week-3, priority:high

title: [Client Rule] Implement purchase order (PO/Tender) validation before issuance
body:
## Client Context (Ananya Keshwala - Thornbury Sallow Infrastructure)
Any invoice sent to a ministry/government department must cite a tender number or a purchase order (PO) number. Issuance must be blocked if the PO does not exist or if the invoice total exceeds the PO's remaining balance.

## Tasks
- Create the `PurchaseOrder` entity/repository (PO/Tender number, total amount, remaining balance).
- Add blocking validation when the invoice moves to the `ISSUED` status: verify the PO exists and that `invoice.total <= po.remaining_value`.
- Deduct the invoice amount from the PO's remaining balance at issuance.
- Write tests covering rejection when the PO does not exist or the budget is exceeded.

## Acceptance Criteria (Done when)
- It is impossible to issue a government invoice without a valid PO.
- It is impossible to issue an invoice exceeding the PO's remaining amount.

title: [Feature] Handle issued invoice immutability, credit notes and PDF generation
body:
## Objective
Finalize the invoice lifecycle after issuance and provide a secure downloadable document.

## Tasks
- Make invoices in the `ISSUED` status strictly immutable (no modification/deletion allowed).
- Implement the creation of credit notes (`Credit Note`) linked to an issued invoice.
- Generate the invoice PDF and provide a signed download link (Signed URL).

## Acceptance Criteria (Done when)
- Any attempt to modify an issued invoice is rejected.
- A credit note can be generated and linked to an existing invoice.
- The PDF is generated and accessible via a valid signed link.

title: [CR-1] Estimate the impact and implement scheduled recurring monthly invoices
body:
## Objective
Address change request CR-1 regarding recurring billing.

## Tasks
- Write the impact estimate for `CR-1` in the release notes.
- Create the monthly recurring invoice template model (`RecurringInvoiceTemplate`).
- Implement the scheduler that automatically generates and issues the invoice on the chosen day of the month.

## Acceptance Criteria (Done when)
- The CR-1 impact estimate is included in the release notes.
- The recurring template automatically issues invoices on the scheduled date.
